title: Ray Optics & Optical Instruments — verified two-page formula manifest
curriculum_basis: Supplied CBSE Physics (Code 042), Class XII 2026–27 section; syllabus PDF p. 15. The PDF opening matter also mentions 2025–26, so the Class XII section/footer year is used and the discrepancy is documented.
chapter_basis: Supplied NCERT Class XII Physics, Chapter 9, Ray Optics and Optical Instruments; reprint 2026–27, printed pp. 221–254.
reference_use_rule: Visual/layout reference only. Neither image is authoritative for formula correctness, completeness, or notation. Use the supplied NCERT and syllabus as the source hierarchy, then this manifest.

shared_notation.u: signed object distance from the mirror pole or lens optical centre
shared_notation.v: signed image distance from the mirror pole or lens optical centre
shared_notation.h_o, h_i: object and image heights; signed by the vertical Cartesian convention
shared_notation.n_1, n_2: absolute refractive indices of incident and transmitted media; n_21 = n_2/n_1
shared_notation.f, R, R_1, R_2: signed focal length and signed radii of curvature
shared_notation.i, r, e: angles of incidence, refraction and emergence, measured from the normal
shared_notation.i_c: critical angle for incidence from optically denser to rarer medium
shared_notation.D: least distance of distinct vision; approximately 0.25 m for a normal eye
shared_notation.f_o, f_e: objective and eyepiece focal-length magnitudes in the instrument magnifying-power expressions
shared_notation.L: compound microscope tube length: separation of objective second focal point and eyepiece first focal point
shared_notation.P: lens power in dioptres; P=1/f when f is in metres
shared_notation.m, M: linear magnification or angular magnifying power, explicitly identified per entry

cartesian_sign_convention: Measure from mirror pole or lens optical centre. Along incident light is positive; opposite is negative. Heights above the principal axis are positive; below are negative. For the ordinary real-object arrangement u<0. Concave mirror f,R<0; convex mirror f,R>0. Converging lens f>0; diverging lens f<0. Assign no guessed sign to unknown quantities. Telescope angular magnification uses positive focal-length magnitudes and a leading minus to encode inversion.

formulas.topic: 9.2 Reflection of Light by Spherical Mirrors
formulas.name: Law of reflection
formulas.symbols: i: incidence angle; r: reflection angle, both measured from the normal.
formulas.units: Angles; dimensionless in radians (degrees commonly used in school problems).
formulas.conditions: At a reflecting surface; incident ray, reflected ray and normal are coplanar.
formulas.sign_note: Not a signed-distance equation.
formulas.source: NCERT printed pp. 222, 247; syllabus PDF p. 15; supplement photo 20261029_163816.jpg.

formulas.topic: 9.2 Reflection of Light by Spherical Mirrors
formulas.name: Focal length of a spherical mirror
formulas.symbols: f: focal length; R: radius of curvature.
formulas.units: m (or one consistent length unit).
formulas.conditions: Spherical mirror; paraxial rays / small-aperture approximation.
formulas.sign_note: Concave mirror f,R<0; convex mirror f,R>0.

formulas.topic: 9.2 Reflection of Light by Spherical Mirrors
formulas.name: Mirror equation
formulas.symbols: u,v: signed object and image distances; f: focal length; R: radius of curvature.
formulas.units: u,v,f,R in m or a consistent common length unit.
formulas.conditions: Spherical mirror, paraxial image formation.
formulas.sign_note: Apply signed Cartesian distances for all mirror types and real/virtual images.

formulas.topic: 9.2 Reflection of Light by Spherical Mirrors
formulas.name: Mirror linear magnification
formulas.symbols: h_i,h_o: signed image/object heights; v,u: signed image/object distances.
formulas.units: m is dimensionless; heights and distances in a common length unit.
formulas.conditions: Spherical mirror image formation.
formulas.sign_note: For an ordinary real object: m<0 real/inverted; m>0 virtual/erect. Supplement alternatives m=f/(f-u)=(f-v)/f are equivalent and consolidated here.

formulas.name: Absolute refractive index from speed
formulas.symbols: c: speed of light in vacuum; v_light: speed of light in the medium.
formulas.units: Both speeds in m s^-1; n dimensionless.
formulas.conditions: Specified transparent medium and wavelength.
formulas.sign_note: Supplementary page expresses this definition; no sign convention applies.
formulas.source: Supplement photo 20261029_163351.jpg; NCERT printed pp. 228–229 discusses optical density/speed.

formulas.name: Wavelength form of refractive index
formulas.symbols: lambda_0: vacuum wavelength; lambda: wavelength in medium.
formulas.units: Wavelengths in m; n dimensionless.
formulas.conditions: Frequency remains unchanged at a stationary interface; use the selected wavelength.
formulas.sign_note: Equivalent wavelength form, not a separate physical rule from RO-005.

formulas.name: Snell's law and relative refractive index
formulas.expression: n_21 = sin(i)/sin(r) = n_2/n_1; equivalently n_1 sin(i) = n_2 sin(r)
formulas.symbols: i,r: incidence/refraction angles from normal; n_1,n_2: indices before/after interface; n_21=n_2/n_1.
formulas.units: Angles; refractive indices dimensionless.
formulas.conditions: Refraction at an interface at a specified wavelength.
formulas.sign_note: Keep medium labels consistent; incident ray, refracted ray and normal are coplanar.

formulas.name: Reciprocal and chained relative indices
formulas.symbols: n_ab: refractive index of medium a relative to medium b.
formulas.units: Dimensionless.
formulas.conditions: Same wavelength and consistent medium indexing.
formulas.sign_note: Equivalent to the reciprocal/product convention printed in the NCERT text.

formulas.name: Apparent depth
formulas.expression: n_21 approximately real_depth/apparent_depth; for viewing from air, apparent_depth approximately real_depth/n
formulas.symbols: n_21: index of viewed medium relative to observer medium; real/apparent depths.
formulas.units: Depths in m; index dimensionless.
formulas.conditions: Plane interface, near-normal viewing / paraxial approximation.
formulas.sign_note: Approximate result; not an oblique-viewing formula.

formulas.name: Lateral shift through a parallel-sided slab
formulas.symbols: t: slab thickness; d: lateral displacement; i,r: incident/refracted angles for slab geometry.
formulas.units: t,d in m; angles in radians or degrees used consistently.
formulas.conditions: Plane-parallel slab; emergent ray parallel to incident ray.
formulas.sign_note: No net angular deviation in an ideal plane-parallel slab.
formulas.source: Supplement photo 20261029_163351.jpg; NCERT discusses and illustrates the shift at printed p. 229.

formulas.name: Apparent rise/shift of a layer
formulas.expression: apparent_shift = t(1-1/n); for stacked layers total_apparent_shift approximately sum_j t_j(1-1/n_j)
formulas.symbols: t_j: layer thickness; n_j: layer index relative to viewing medium (air assumed 1 in guide form).
formulas.units: Thickness and shift in m; index dimensionless.
formulas.conditions: Parallel interfaces and near-normal view.
formulas.sign_note: Equivalent to apparent-depth relation under the stated viewing conditions.

formulas.name: Critical angle
formulas.expression: sin(i_c) = n_r/n_d; for rarer medium air, n_d approximately 1/sin(i_c)
formulas.symbols: i_c: critical angle; n_d,n_r: indices of denser and rarer media.
formulas.units: Angle; indices dimensionless.
formulas.conditions: Incidence from optically denser to rarer medium; refracted ray has r=90 degrees at criticality.
formulas.sign_note: General form avoids silently assuming air as the rarer medium.

formulas.name: TIR conditions
formulas.symbols: n_d,n_r: indices of denser/rarer media; i incidence angle; i_c critical angle.
formulas.units: Indices dimensionless; angles measured from normal.
formulas.conditions: Light travels from optically denser to optically rarer medium.
formulas.sign_note: At i=i_c the refracted ray grazes the interface; TIR occurs for i>i_c.

formulas.name: Optical-fibre index condition
formulas.symbols: n_core,n_cladding: refractive indices of fibre core and cladding.
formulas.units: Dimensionless.
formulas.conditions: Guiding by repeated TIR at core–cladding interface.
formulas.sign_note: Qualitative condition, not an acceptance-angle formula.
formulas.source: NCERT printed pp. 231–232; syllabus PDF p. 15.

formulas.name: Spherical refracting surface equation
formulas.symbols: n_1,n_2: incident/transmitted indices; u,v: signed object/image distances from vertex; R: signed radius.
formulas.units: u,v,R in m; indices dimensionless.
formulas.conditions: Spherical interface; small aperture/paraxial rays.
formulas.sign_note: Use NCERT Cartesian convention; R positive when centre of curvature is in positive incident-light direction.

formulas.name: Surface power
formulas.symbols: n_1,n_2: indices across interface; R: signed radius.
formulas.units: R in m; P_s in m^-1 (dioptre); indices dimensionless.
formulas.conditions: Paraxial spherical interface.
formulas.sign_note: Supplementary surface power; not the complete power of a thick lens.

formulas.name: First principal focal length of a spherical surface
formulas.symbols: n_1,n_2: incident/transmitted indices; R: signed radius; f_1: first principal focal length.
formulas.units: R,f_1 in m; indices dimensionless.
formulas.conditions: Same paraxial spherical interface.
formulas.sign_note: Signed focal length and radius under NCERT Cartesian convention.

formulas.name: Second principal focal length of a spherical surface
formulas.symbols: n_1,n_2: incident/transmitted indices; R: signed radius; f_1,f_2: principal focal lengths.
formulas.units: R,f_1,f_2 in m; indices dimensionless.
formulas.conditions: Same paraxial spherical interface.
formulas.sign_note: Ratio is a consequence of RO-017; signed radii are essential.

formulas.name: Lens-maker formula in surrounding medium
formulas.symbols: n_2: lens index; n_1: surrounding-medium index; R_1,R_2: signed surface radii.
formulas.units: f,R_1,R_2 in m; indices dimensionless.
formulas.conditions: Thin lens, paraxial rays, homogeneous surrounding medium.
formulas.sign_note: Apply signed Cartesian radii; for surrounding index unity this reduces to RO-020.

formulas.name: Lens-maker formula in air
formulas.symbols: n: lens refractive index relative to air; R_1,R_2: signed radii.
formulas.units: f,R_1,R_2 in m; n dimensionless.
formulas.conditions: Thin lens in air, paraxial rays.
formulas.sign_note: f>0 converging; f<0 diverging lens under standard signed radii.

formulas.name: Thin-lens equation
formulas.symbols: u,v: signed object/image distances; f: signed focal length.
formulas.units: m or one consistent common length unit.
formulas.conditions: Thin lens, paraxial approximation.
formulas.sign_note: Applies to converging/diverging lenses and real/virtual images with signed distances.

formulas.name: Lens linear magnification
formulas.symbols: h_i,h_o: signed image/object heights; v,u: signed image/object distances.
formulas.units: m dimensionless; heights/distances in a common length unit.
formulas.conditions: Thin lens image formation.
formulas.sign_note: For usual real-object setup m>0 erect/virtual and m<0 inverted/real; do not use the mirror minus sign.

formulas.name: Lens power
formulas.symbols: P: signed power; f_m: focal length in metres; f_cm: focal length in centimetres.
formulas.units: P in dioptres (m^-1).
formulas.conditions: Thin lens as prescribed in air; retain focal-length sign.
formulas.sign_note: P positive converging, negative diverging.
formulas.verification: Verified; centimetre form is unit conversion

formulas.topic: 9.5.4 Combination of Thin Lenses in Contact
formulas.name: Equivalent focal length and power, lenses in contact
formulas.symbols: F: effective focal length; f_j,P_j: individual lens focal lengths and powers.
formulas.units: F,f_j in m; powers in D.
formulas.conditions: Thin lenses in contact/coincident optical centres; common axis and medium.
formulas.sign_note: Algebraic power sum; retain signs of converging/diverging lenses.

formulas.topic: 9.5.4 Combination of Thin Lenses in Contact
formulas.name: Magnification of lens combination
formulas.symbols: m_j: signed linear magnification of each lens.
formulas.units: Dimensionless.
formulas.conditions: Sequential image formation by a lens combination.
formulas.sign_note: Keep each image-orientation sign.

formulas.name: Prism geometry
formulas.symbols: A: prism refracting angle; r_1,r_2: internal refraction angles.
formulas.units: Angles (radians in SI; degrees common).
formulas.conditions: Ray traverses the two refracting faces.
formulas.sign_note: Angles measured from face normals per NCERT geometry.

formulas.name: Prism deviation
formulas.symbols: i: incidence; e: emergence; A: prism angle; delta: deviation.
formulas.units: Angles.
formulas.conditions: Ray refracts through both prism faces.
formulas.sign_note: Total deviation is sum of deviation at each face.

formulas.name: Minimum deviation condition and prism refractive index
formulas.expression: At minimum deviation: i=e, r_1=r_2=A/2; n_21 = sin[(A+delta_m)/2]/sin(A/2)
formulas.symbols: A: prism angle; delta_m: minimum deviation; n_21: prism index relative to surrounding medium.
formulas.units: Angles; index dimensionless.
formulas.conditions: Symmetric path at minimum deviation; internal ray parallel to prism base.
formulas.sign_note: Use one angle unit consistently.

formulas.name: Thin-prism deviation
formulas.symbols: delta: deviation; n_21: prism index relative to surrounding medium; A: prism angle.
formulas.units: A and delta in radians for the small-angle approximation.
formulas.conditions: Thin prism, small A and small deviations.
formulas.sign_note: Do not use as the exact relation for a large-angle prism.

formulas.name: Angular magnification definition
formulas.symbols: theta_i: angle subtended at eye by image; theta_o: angle subtended by unaided object.
formulas.units: Angles in radians; M dimensionless.
formulas.conditions: Small-angle paraxial optical-instrument approximation.
formulas.sign_note: For telescopes a signed value can record image inversion; magnitude is often quoted.

formulas.name: Simple microscope, final image at near point
formulas.symbols: D: least distance of distinct vision; f: converging magnifier focal length.
formulas.units: D,f in the same length unit; M dimensionless.
formulas.conditions: Final virtual image at near point; paraxial model.
formulas.sign_note: D approximately 25 cm for a normal eye.

formulas.name: Simple microscope, final image at infinity
formulas.symbols: D: least distance of distinct vision; f: converging magnifier focal length.
formulas.units: D,f in same length unit; M dimensionless.
formulas.conditions: Final image at infinity / relaxed eye.
formulas.sign_note: D approximately 25 cm for a normal eye.

formulas.name: Objective magnification
formulas.symbols: u_o,v_o: signed object/image distances for objective; L: microscope tube length; f_o: objective focal length.
formulas.units: u_o,v_o,L,f_o in same length unit; m_o dimensionless.
formulas.conditions: Objective forms a real intermediate image; L/f_o form is NCERT near-focus approximation.
formulas.sign_note: Negative sign indicates inverted intermediate image.

formulas.name: Eyepiece magnification, final image at near point
formulas.symbols: D: near point; f_e: eyepiece focal length.
formulas.units: D,f_e in same length unit; M_e dimensionless.
formulas.conditions: Eyepiece as simple microscope; final virtual image at near point.
formulas.sign_note: D approximately 25 cm for a normal eye.

formulas.name: Eyepiece magnification, final image at infinity
formulas.symbols: D: near point; f_e: eyepiece focal length.
formulas.units: D,f_e in same length unit; M_e dimensionless.
formulas.conditions: Final image at infinity / relaxed eye.
formulas.sign_note: Final compound microscope image remains inverted due to objective.

formulas.name: Total magnifying power, final image at near point
formulas.symbols: m_o: signed objective magnification; M_e: eyepiece angular magnification; D,f_e,u_o,v_o as above.
formulas.units: All lengths in same unit; M dimensionless.
formulas.conditions: Compound microscope, final virtual image at near point.
formulas.sign_note: Equivalent approximate form -(L/f_o)(1+D/f_e) if objective approximation is used.
formulas.source: Supplement photo 20261029_163708.jpg; consistent with NCERT printed p. 244.

formulas.name: Total magnifying power, final image at infinity
formulas.symbols: L: tube length; f_o,f_e: objective and eyepiece focal lengths; D: near point.
formulas.units: All lengths in same unit; M dimensionless.
formulas.conditions: Final image at infinity; NCERT microscope tube-length approximation.
formulas.sign_note: Negative sign indicates final image inverted; quote |M| for positive magnifying-power magnitude.

formulas.name: Telescope angular magnification
formulas.symbols: f_o,f_e: positive focal-length magnitudes of objective and eyepiece; M signed angular magnification.
formulas.units: Focal lengths in same length unit; M dimensionless.
formulas.conditions: Distant object, normal adjustment/final image at infinity, paraxial telescope.
formulas.sign_note: Leading minus denotes inverted final image. For reflecting telescope, f_o is magnitude of concave objective mirror focal length.

formulas.name: Telescope length in normal adjustment
formulas.symbols: s_tel: separation of objective and eyepiece focal planes; f_o,f_e: positive focal-length magnitudes.
formulas.units: All lengths in same unit.
formulas.conditions: Astronomical telescope in normal adjustment; final image at infinity.
formulas.sign_note: For reflecting arrangement use the objective mirror focal-length magnitude.
formulas.source: NCERT printed p. 245 description; supplement photo 20261029_163724.jpg.
